title: Śivena me santiṣṭhasva: stay with me
theme: The one addressed as ‘sacrifice’ is asked to stay with the speaker, bringing welfare, comfort, prosperity and the radiance of sacred learning, and is given homage three times.

words.meaning: with what is auspicious, with welfare

sandhi.type: a + ṛ; final m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: yajñasya + ṛddhim → yajñasyarddhim: a and ṛ fuse into ar; ṛddhim anu: the m is joined to the vowel.
santiṣṭhasva + upa → santiṣṭhasvopa: a and u fuse into o.

sandhi.type: visarga after a before a vowel other than a
sandhi.rule: namaḥ + upa → nama upa: the visarga is dropped and the vowels stay apart.

samasa.meaning: the lustre that comes of sacred knowledge

morphology.note: Middle imperative of √sthā with sam-, ‘stay, remain, be established’; the root’s present stem is tiṣṭha-.
Vocative: the sacrifice is addressed as a person; the anonymous commentator takes it as the Lord whose form is every sacrifice.

translation.literal: Abide with me with welfare; abide with me with comfort; abide with me with prosperity; abide with me with the lustre of sacred knowledge; abide following the success of the sacrifice. Close to you, O sacrifice, homage; close to you, homage; close to you, homage.
translation.readable: Stay with me, bringing welfare; stay with me, bringing comfort; stay with me, bringing prosperity; stay with me, bringing the radiance of sacred learning; stay, as the sacrifice prospers. Homage to you, O Sacrifice, close at hand — homage to you, homage to you.

anvaya: यज्ञ शिवेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व । स्योनेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व । सुभूतेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व । ब्रह्मवर्चसेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व । यज्ञस्य ऋद्धिम् अनु सन्तिष्ठस्व । ते उप नमः । उप ते नमः । उप ते नमः
syntax: Five commands with the same verb, santiṣṭhasva: four with an instrumental of what is to accompany the one addressed and the enclitic me, the fifth with the postposition anu. Then three nominal clauses, upa te … namaḥ, the first with the vocative yajña.

ambiguities.note: The vocative yajña may address the rite itself or a deity identified with it; the anonymous commentator addresses the Lord whose form is every sacrifice, the supreme self («हे भगवन्»).
Genitive or dative ‘with me / for me’; the anonymous commentator takes it as ‘in my house’.

metre.name: prose
metre.note: A single yajus formula of 62 syllables.

beginner: This is a request to stay. The speaker asks ‘you’ to remain with him, bringing welfare, comfort, prosperity and the radiance that comes with sacred learning, and to stay as the sacrifice succeeds. Then he offers homage three times, each time saying ‘close to you’. The one addressed is called ‘sacrifice’. The anonymous commentator, the only one in this edition who explains the line, takes this as the Lord whose form is every sacrifice, and reads the request as asking him to dwell in the speaker’s house so that the speaker may share those qualities. He explains the threefold homage as a sign of great respect. The edition reports this as his reading.
analogy: Like a host at the door asking a valued guest not to leave yet, and naming the good things the guest has brought into the house.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It asks the one addressed to stay with the speaker with welfare, comfort, prosperity and the lustre of sacred knowledge, and to stay following the success of the sacrifice; then it says three times ‘homage, close to you’, the first time addressing ‘sacrifice’.

commentary.q: Who is addressed, and what is asked?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator: the Lord, whose form is all sacrifice («हे यज्ञ सर्वयज्ञस्वरूप»), asked to dwell in the house with welfare and the rest («शिवेन कल्याणप्रदानेन सह मे गृहे»), so that the speaker may share those qualities («एवंगुणवति त्वयि मद्गृह उपस्थिते सत्यहमप्येवंविधगुणवान्भूयासमिति प्रार्थयितुराशयः»).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The repetition, says the anonymous commentator, is for great respect: «अत्यादरार्थमाम्रेडितम्».

schools.disagreement: No Vedānta-school commentary on this text is in the edition’s sources: Raṅgarāmānuja’s is not available, and the commentaries present (the anonymous bhāṣya, Sāyaṇa, Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara) are ritual and Vedic explanations, not school readings. Only the anonymous commentator explains this formula in the edition’s sources.

contemporary.text: The formula is phrased as an invitation to stay rather than a demand to give: it names what the guest brings and asks for its presence. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: Which of the four things named — welfare, comfort, prosperity, the radiance of learning — would you most want to ‘stay’ in your home?
reflect.deeper: Why might the text address ‘the sacrifice’ as someone who can stay or leave?
reflect.practice: Name one good quality you would like to have stay with you, and one thing you could do to keep it.

references.text: No comment of Sāyaṇa or Bhāskara on this anuvāka is in the edition’s files.

flags.note: The Tirupati e-text lacks part of the series (from स्योनेन to सुभूत…), and prints शुचिः, the last word of 10.76, at the start of this anuvāka; the collation leaves the omission for review. The Ānandāśrama pariśiṣṭa text reads संतिष्ठास्व once, classed as its error.
Only one commentary explains this anuvāka in the edition’s sources.
